propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times, each invoking git config user.name via subprocess, consuming 47.79s of the 93-108s total runtime
The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging 3,000 times for CREATE events, rescanning the same staging root within each batch while items remain unpublished, consuming 15.94s
An import-scoped, contextvar-based author cache keyed by fallback can reduce git-config reads to one per import while preserving interactive per-call behavior and unknown/fallback parity
A per-batch stale-staging sweep flag can reduce sweeps to one per first new-ticket CREATE in each bounded batch, retaining direct caller and empty/existing-only batch behavior
The optimization must preserve exactly 24 crash-safe commits, >=10x commit-count reduction, 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, idempotency, rollback, and resume semantics from left-changeful-mamba

Controlled A/B testing with logical collaborators replacing only the git-config and sweep mechanisms achieved identical state and commits in 16.4s versus 77.2s baseline, isolating 60.8s (78.8%) of avoidable cost
